official.description: Trinity College Dublin awards Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarships to exceptional international students who have received a course offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme, as a one-time tuition-fee reduction between EUR 2,000 and EUR 5,000 depending on region. Applicants must hold non-EU fee status billed at the non-EU rate, and applications are assessed on a rolling basis against the deadline for their region.
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page itself publishes no English test requirement. Trinity requires all applicants to provide official evidence of English proficiency, with the majority of undergraduate and postgraduate courses accepting Band B: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band, TOEFL iBT 90 overall with 21 in each section, Duolingo 120 overall, PTE Academic 69 overall, or Cambridge Advanced/Proficiency 180 overall. Postgraduate applicants whose primary degree was completed through the medium of English may request an exemption from the course director/coordinator.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition discount rather than a scholarship: at EUR 2,000-5,000 it is deducted from your fee bill only, so Dublin rent, flights, visa costs and health insurance all remain on you. It pays out only if you already hold and then fully accept a Trinity postgraduate taught offer while being billed at the non-EU rate, so it cannot fund your application - it rewards admission you have already won. Check the exempt disciplines before you spend any effort: business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics applicants must use the E3 or business-masters routes, and Chinese applicants must use the Claddagh scheme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong-grades non-EU applicants who already hold a taught master's offer at Trinity in a non-exempt discipline.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme is not in the exempt list (business, engineering, natural sciences, computer science and statistics) before doing anything else
Secure your Trinity offer and then fully accept it - the award is paid only to awardees who have fully accepted
Draft the 'how you will contribute to the Trinity community' statement early: it is the only substantial written piece in an otherwise short form
Diarise your own region's closing date and submit weeks ahead, because assessment is rolling and there is no second chance after it
common_rejection_risks: Holding EU fee status (or non-EU residency with EU fee status) - the award keys off non-EU fee billing, not nationality or where you live
Missing the regional cut-off while waiting for a Trinity admission decision that only arrives close to the deadline
Applying from an exempt discipline and assuming Global Excellence still applies
A Chinese applicant submitting to Global Excellence instead of the Claddagh Postgraduate Scholarship
Assuming silence means pending - Trinity states unsuccessful applicants are not contacted individually
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remainder of non-EU tuition above the EUR 5,000 cap, Dublin living costs, flights, immigration and health insurance costs - none of which this award touches.
document_audit: No transcripts, references or certificates are requested at the form stage, so there is nothing to have certified or stamped in advance
If the online form is blocked in your country you must reach the Trinity Regional Manager for your region for an alternative paper form - do not assume emailing central admissions will substitute
The community-contribution statement is the only free-text field, so a generic answer here is easy to spot against regionally diverse competition
alerts: All four published regional deadlines for the 2026/2027 round (1 April to 15 July 2026) have passed, so nothing can be submitted for that intake
If Trinity does not contact you after your regional closing date, treat the application as unsuccessful
The award covers year one only - from year two your full non-EU fee returns
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the short online form linked from the scholarship page once you hold an offer; Trinity assesses on a rolling basis and notifies winners after each regional closing date.

official.citizenship_residency: "Applicants from any country may hold a Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship" but fall into Category 1 (national of an EU member state including the Republic of Ireland, or Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, the United Kingdom or Ukraine, AND ordinarily resident in such a state for a continuous period of three of the five years preceding 1 September 2025) or Category 2 (all other applicants).
official.international_eligibility: Yes - Category 2 applicants from outside those states are eligible, although Research Ireland states that only a proportion of scholarships will be made to exceptional Category 2 applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: "funding across all disciplines, from archaeology to zoology" and "awards for bottom-up, non-directed research", with the 2026 strategic funding partner themes being the Environmental Protection Agency, the Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth, the Department of Foreign Affairs and Met Eireann - applicants may apply for one theme only.
official.research_requirement: An original, bottom-up research project written by the applicant, distinct from any other proposal, supported by a primary supervisor at an Eligible Research Body in Ireland; the project "is currently or has previously been funded either in full, or in part, by Research Ireland or any other funding agency" is ineligible.
official.duration: "The duration of a Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship ranges from one to four years depending on the type of degree being pursued" - new entrants: 2 years for a research master's and 4 years for a doctoral degree; 1 year (research master's) or 3 years (doctoral) for applicants who completed no more than the first year.
official.description: The Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme is an established national initiative, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science and managed by Research Ireland, awarding individual prestigious research scholarships in the name of the applicant. Worth up to EUR 34,000 per annum - a EUR 25,000 stipend, up to EUR 5,750 towards fees and EUR 3,250 of eligible direct costs - for one to four years of full-time research in any discipline, selected by international independent expert peer review.
official.english_requirement: "Research Ireland does not require English Language Certificates. However, you should check what (if any) are the English language requirements determined by the Eligible research body in which you will be enrolled for research master's or PhD." Applications "will only be accepted in either the Irish or English language."

applicant_utility.summary: This is a named personal research award rather than a university scholarship: you apply through an Irish Eligible Research Body and the money follows you, so securing a willing primary supervisor months before a call opens is the real entry ticket. The value is substantial at up to EUR 34,000 a year - stipend, fees and research costs - but the grant must be accepted in full across all three headings, so there is no partial-award option. With an 18% average success rate, and only 2-3% for applicants outside the EU/EEA residency category, treat this as a multi-year campaign rather than a single submission.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving new entrants to a research master's or PhD at an Irish Eligible Research Body who already have, or can build, a strong relationship with a prospective primary supervisor.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach your prospective primary supervisor well before the call opens - Research Ireland will not help you find one, and each supervisor can back only one applicant
Register an ORCID before the call opens, since it is needed on the application
Ask your research office to confirm your Category (1 or 2) and your date of first registration against the eligibility table before you start writing
Plan around three separate online closing dates - yours, your supervisor's and your research office's - and submit hours early on the closing day because of server load
common_rejection_risks: Submitting more than one application in a call, or a supervisor endorsing two applicants - both make every affected application ineligible
Having a date of first registration earlier than the cut-off (before 1 September 2025 for the 2026 call)
Uploading a CV, publication files or any extra attachment - additional materials are explicitly disqualifying
Already holding a master's degree when applying for a research master's, or holding any previous Research Ireland scholarship
Canvassing on the applicant's behalf, which is grounds for ineligibility
Word-limit overruns or an incomplete application, both of which are screened out before any peer review happens
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any non-EU fee differential above the EUR 5,750 contribution plus the EUR 4,000 non-EU top-up, and any travel, training or dissemination costs beyond the EUR 3,250 direct-costs allowance.
document_audit: Transcripts must be stamped, signed official documents showing overall result, graduation date and awarding institution - if the printed overall result does not match the form exactly, the conditional offer is withdrawn
Uploaded PDFs must not reveal your gender; use initials rather than first names for publications in the bibliography
Never send medical or passport documentation to Research Ireland unless asked - career-break evidence goes to your research office
List all publications, co-authored included, inside the Research Achievements field; do not attach publication files
alerts: The 2026 call closed on 23 October 2025, outcomes were announced at the end of April 2026 and awards started on 1 September 2026 - nothing is open now, so use the gap to build the supervisor relationship for the next round
The grant must be accepted in full including all three budget headings; partial acceptance is not permitted under any circumstances
Unsuccessful applicants receive only the score assigned by the international assessment board - no qualitative feedback and no correspondence about individual assessments
Scholars must be resident in the Republic of Ireland within reasonable travelling distance of the host body, so relocation is part of the commitment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit through the Research Ireland online system by the applicant deadline, then chase your primary supervisor and your research office to complete their own online endorsements by their later deadlines - a missing endorsement at the cut-off makes the application ineligible.
